title: NEW MSFS 2024 Aircraft: Fokker 70/100, Hawker 800XP, F-111 + warning!
description:
Are you looking to expand your Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 hangar this week, or are you trying to decide which new add-ons are worth your investment? Today, we are breaking down a massive slate of high-profile Marketplace releases spanning study-level regional airliners and luxury corporate jets to supersonic swing-wing tactical bombers, floatplanes, and essential cockpit utilities.

In this deep-dive marketplace breakdown, we cover flight dynamics, system fidelity, native MSFS 2024 integration, and pricing models to see which add-ons deserve a spot on your virtual flight line:

✈️ COMMERCIAL & CORPORATE AVIATION
We start with Just Flight's flagship F70 and F100 Professional—fully customized study-level regional twinjets featuring AFCAS autoland, custom hydraulic/fuel architectures, SimBrief and Navigraph EFB integration, and fully modeled interactive cabins and galleys (with bundle pricing evaluated). Then, we step into the corporate flight deck of FlightFX's native Hawker 800XP, exploring its Pro Line 21 suite, DEEC engine logic, custom thrust reversers, and accumulating engine character. We also issue an essential buyer advisory regarding Captain Sim’s E-767 AWACS and its underlying default systems.

⚡ FAST MILITARY & TACTICAL FLIGHT
Ready for Mach 2 low-level runs? We inspect the iconic General Dynamics F-111E Aardvark tactical bomber by Golden Key Studio, featuring operational variable-sweep wings, afterburners, and authentic cockpit instrumentation. Next, we review Embraer's A-29 Super Tucano turboprop attack trainer, featuring custom MFDs, HUD, UFCP, and multi-livery loadouts.

🌲 ULTRALIGHT TOURING, ROTORCRAFT & FLIGHT DECK UTILITIES
For bush and water flying, FSReborn brings the TL Ultralight Sirius / TL-3000 series with native CFD floats, prop physics, CAPS rescue systems, and dual GTN 750 integration. Finally, we explore productivity and immersion updates: the built-in MSFS 2024 EFB Challenging Weather Finder app, King Air 350i custom flight deck textures, the HR Simyard H125 multi-mission sling pack (firefighting buckets & cargo gear), and Echo 9 Audio's high-fidelity sound overhaul for the Black Square TBM 850.

Which of these releases are you taking up first? Setting up regional schedules in the Fokker twins, cruising high in the Hawker 800XP, or sweeping the wings on the F-111? Let us know in the comments below!

If you find these marketplace breakdowns helpful, don't forget to hit the like button, subscribe for weekly flight sim coverage, and clear skies on your next flight!
